bib.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning

question: Can parameter-efficient fine-tuning on a few labeled examples beat few-shot in-context learning in accuracy and compute cost?
hypothesis: Adding unlikelihood loss will improve rank classification because the model is trained to assign lower probability to incorrect choices.
contributions: Rigorous comparison of few-shot ICL and PEFT showing PEFT is more accurate and far cheaper
(IA)3, a PEFT method that rescales keys, values and FFN inner activations with learned vectors
T-Few, a fixed recipe (T0 + (IA)3 + pre-training + LUL + LLN) needing no per-task tuning, with super-human accuracy on RAFT

method.summary: Design T-Few on T0-3B with 5 few-shot subsamples of 9 held-out T0 datasets: add unlikelihood and length-normalized losses, compare 12 PEFT settings, introduce (IA)3 and pre-train it on T0's mixture. Apply the fixed recipe to T0 11B and compare with ICL baselines and on RAFT, with FLOP-based cost estimates.
method.task: few-shot classification and multiple choice (rank classification)

datasets.name: Held-out T0 tasks (COPA, H-SWAG, Story Cloze, ANLI R1-R3, CB, RTE, WSC, Winogrande, WiC)
datasets.size: 20 to 70 few-shot training examples per dataset (same counts as Brown et al.); median 41 shots
datasets.split: five few-shot subsets from different seeds; test set, or validation set when test labels not public
datasets.preprocessing: P3 prompt templates, random template per example per step

datasets.name: RAFT
datasets.size: 11 tasks, 50 training examples each, no validation set, hidden test labels
datasets.preprocessing: standard prompts released with dataset; Banking 77: unlikelihood off, labels in input, '.' replaced by ','

models.name: T0-3B
models.init_from: T5 fine-tuned on multitask prompted mixture

models.name: T0 (11B)
models.init_from: T5 fine-tuned on multitask prompted mixture

other.note: ensemble ICL, one-shot per training example, predictions averaged; EleutherAI eval harness
numbers copied from Brown et al.

training.objective: sum of L_LM + L_UL (unlikelihood on incorrect choices) + L_LN (softmax CE over length-normalized log-probs), unweighted
training.hardware: T0-3B: 48GB A6000; T0 11B: 80GB A100 (DataCrunch); (IA)3 pre-training 1 day on 4 A6000 / 4 A100
training.wall_clock: about half an hour per task on one A100 (~$2 on Azure)
training.seeds: 5 few-shot subsets by seed; training-seed count not stated

other.design_runs_other_peft: FT/BitFit/LayerNorm 300 steps lr 3e-4; Adapter 500 steps 3e-3, reduction 32; Compacter(++) 500 steps 3e-3, n=4; prompt tuning 1000 steps lr 3e-1, 10 or 100 prompts; prefix tuning 1000 steps 3e-3, MLP hidden 512; FishMask 1500 steps 3e-4, 0.2% or 0.02%; Intrinsic SAID 3000 steps 3e-2; LoRA rank 4, init scale 0.01, 1000 steps 3e-3
other.ia3_params: L(dk+dv+dff) encoder, L(2dk+2dv+dff) decoder; init to ones; 540K on T0-3B

inference.samples: median accuracy over all P3 prompt templates and 5 few-shot subsets

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: rank classification correct if highest-ranked choice is correct; median across templates and few-shot subsets; mean across datasets in headline numbers

metrics.name: FLOPs per example
metrics.definition: Kaplan estimates: decoder 2N/6N per token inference/training, enc-dec N/3N; 41 shots x 98 tokens + 103

baselines: BitFit, LayerNorm, Adapter, Compacter, Compacter++, prompt tuning, prefix tuning, FISH Mask, Intrinsic SAID, LoRA
RAFT: Human baseline, PET, SetFit, GPT-3
eval.protocol: median and IQR over 5 few-shot subsets; no per-dataset tuning in T-Few; GPT-3 numbers not rerun

results.claim: T-Few (T0 11B) beats few-shot ICL with GPT-3 175B on held-out T0 tasks
results.setup: Nine held-out T0 datasets, T0 11B, 5 few-shot subsets, median

results.claim: T-Few matches higher accuracy at about 1,000x fewer inference FLOPs than GPT-3 175B ICL
results.setup: 41 shots x 98 tokens + 103; Kaplan FLOP estimates
results.quote: T-Few requires 11e9×103 = 1.1e12 FLOPs, whereas few-shot ICL with GPT-3 175B requires 2×175e9× (41 × 98 + 103) = 1.4e15 FLOPs

results.claim: Training T-Few costs about 20x the FLOPs of one GPT-3 175B ICL example (2.7e16 FLOPs)
results.quote: this is only about 20 times larger than the FLOPs

results.claim: T-Few reaches state of the art on RAFT and beats the human baseline
results.setup: RAFT 11 tasks, 50 train examples each, hidden test, T-Few unchanged

results.claim: (IA)3 is the only PEFT method that beats full-model fine-tuning on T0-3B
results.quote: (IA)3 is the only method that attains higher accuracy than the full-model-ﬁne-tuning baseline

results.claim: (IA)3 adds 540K parameters on T0-3B vs LoRA 9.1M
results.table: Table 4 (appendix D), row (IA)3, column # of Param

results.claim: Adding L_LN raises full fine-tuning accuracy 60.7 to 62.71; adding L_UL too gives 63.3
results.quote: adding LLN improves the accuracy from 60.7% to 62.71% and including both LUL and LLN provides a further improvement to 63.3%
results.note: 62.71 printed with two decimals, others one

results.setup: T0-3B, 100k steps batch 16 on T0 mixture
results.quote: pre-training improves ﬁne-tuned accuracy from 64.6 to 65.8

results.claim: Ablation on T0 11B: no pre-training 70.8; no LUL/LLN 68.3; neither 69.7
results.note: text says removing LUL+LLN decreases 4.1% and both 2.5%; table gives 72.4 vs 68.3 vs 69.7

results.claim: Gap vs GPT-3 6.7B and 13B on held-out tasks
T0 zero-shot reaches 66.9% and T5+LM ICL 49.6%
Fine-tuned (IA)3 vectors take 4.2 MB on disk vs 16 kB for ICL examples
results.quote: take up 4.2 MB of space on disk

limits: All experiments are classification or multiple choice scored by rank classification; generative tasks left to future work
GPT-3 numbers are copied from Brown et al., not rerun, and their few-shot subsets are undisclosed
FLOPs are a hardware-independent proxy, not latency
Prompt tuning and Compacter results disagree with prior work; authors tried hyperparameters but could not match
Design choices were tuned on T0-3B with the same nine datasets later used for evaluation on T0 11B
